questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) He go  (B) to school  (C) every day.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: "He" is third person singular, so the verb should be goes.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) The children  (B) is playing  (C) in the garden.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Children is plural, so are playing.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) She has  (B) a good  (C) knowledges.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Knowledge is uncountable and has no plural form.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) I am  (B) agree with  (C) your opinion.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Agree is a verb; "am agree" should be "agree".

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) Each of the boys  (B) have  (C) a bicycle.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Each is singular, so has.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) He is  (B) senior than  (C) me.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Senior is followed by to: senior to me.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) Neither of the two  (B) answers are  (C) correct.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Neither is singular, so the verb should be is.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) Hardly had he arrived  (B) when the  (C) train left.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: Hardly had … when.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) I look forward  (B) to meet  (C) you soon.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: After look forward to, use -ing: meeting.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) She prefers  (B) tea than  (C) coffee.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Prefer takes to, not than.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) The news  (B) were  (C) shocking.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: News is uncountable and singular: was.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) Although it rained,  (B) but we  (C) went out.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Although and but should not be used together; remove but.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) He asked me  (B) that where  (C) I lived.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: A reported question takes no "that": where I lived.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) Despite of  (B) the rain,  (C) we went out.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Despite is not followed by of: despite the rain, or in spite of the rain.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) If I  (B) would have known,  (C) I would have told you.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Type 3 conditional: if I had known.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) The quality of  (B) the products  (C) have improved.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: The subject quality is singular, so has improved.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) She has been  (B) living here  (C) since 2010.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous with since is correct.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) Between you  (B) and I,  (C) the plan is risky.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: After a preposition use me: between you and me.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) He is more  (B) smarter  (C) than his brother.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: Double comparative: smarter than, or more intelligent than.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
(A) The teacher  (B) as well as  (C) the students were present.  (D) No error
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the first subject (the teacher): was present.
